title: Kernel discipline: GEN_IV sets iv_set=true before copy_to_user succeeds
description: ioctl_gen_iv() (crypto2dev_fd.c:760-769) calls ops->set_iv() and sets state->iv_set=true at line 764 before the copy_to_user at line 768. If copy_to_user fails (-EFAULT), the function returns -EFAULT to the caller but the provider session already has the IV programmed and iv_set=true. The caller never received the IV bytes, so the session is in a state where: (a) encryption will produce ciphertext with an unknown IV the caller cannot transmit, (b) the caller cannot recover the IV without RESET which destroys the session. The UAPI comment states -EFAULT from write() means the call may be retried, implying atomicity; GEN_IV violates this for the copy_to_user failure case. Fix: perform copy_to_user before set_iv (so iv_set is only set after the user has the IV), or on copy_to_user failure, clear iv_set and call set_iv with zeros to invalidate the programmed IV.
